meanings.note: Singular tutto alone means 'everything'; masculine plural tutti alone means 'everyone'.
Irregular verb; past participle detto, familiar imperative di' (fused in dille, 'tell her').
Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Near demonstrative; colloquially questa alone can refer brusquely to 'this woman / she'.
Invariable feminine noun.
Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Built from pazzo ('crazy').
Negative reply; in se no ('if not'), means 'otherwise'.

examples.trans: Run, otherwise you will be late.

meanings.note: Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Movement away from the speaker or toward a destination.
Used in expressions like va bene, ti va, or andare male.
Opposite of bene; used in andare male ('go badly') and parlare male di ('speak ill of').
Used for fairness (non è giusto), suitability, and tag questions (giusto?, 'right?').

examples.trans: It is not fair like this.

meanings.note: Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
With oraria, la fascia oraria is a television broadcast time slot.
In fascia oraria, describes a broadcast time slot.

examples.trans: We stick to the hourly schedule.

meanings.note: Conversational contrast word, slightly weightier than ma.

examples.trans: It is nice, though it costs too much.

meanings.note: Used impersonally as bisogna + infinitive without a personal subject.
Used both transitively (cambiare canale) and intransitively (le cose cambiano).
Invariable feminine noun ending in a stressed vowel.

examples.trans: We need to change our mindset.

meanings.note: Film, television, or stage director; singular ends in -a for both men and women.

examples.trans: The female director rereads the script.

meanings.note: Both the craft of directing and the directing department on a film crew.
Unstressed 2nd-person plural object pronoun before a verb (vi chiedo, vi ricordo).

examples.trans: I remind you all of the rule.
I will wait for you all outside.

meanings.note: Takes a for the person asked and di before an infinitive.

examples.trans: I ask you for a favour.

meanings.note: Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.

mettere.gloss: to put; to place; to take (time)

meanings.note: Put something somewhere (mettere il cuore); metterci expresses how long something takes.

examples.trans: We put our heart into the work.
How long will it take you?

meanings.note: Default masculine singular definite article before most consonants.
Literal organ and figurative seat of passion (mettere il cuore).

examples.trans: Let us put our heart into the work.

meanings.note: Shortens to buon before most masculine nouns; on set, Buona! approves a take.
Buon lavoro! wishes colleagues a good workday.
Marks destination, location in cities, or indirect recipient.
Links activities and idioms such as giocare a tennis or a presto.
Drops final -e before a surname (il dottor Cane); used in Italy as a respectful title for executives.

examples.text: Il dottor Rossi è al telefono.
examples.trans: Dr Rossi is on the phone.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment, instrument, or attitude.
Con tutto il rispetto ('with all due respect') softens a blunt objection.

examples.text: Con tutto il rispetto, non è giusto.
examples.trans: With all due respect, it is not fair.

meanings.note: Indicates that a situation continues as before.
Indicates repetition or addition.
An unresolved topic or dispute, distinct from una domanda (a spoken question).
Contraction of di + plural article gli before vowels or s + consonant.

examples.trans: He is the head of the electricians.

meanings.note: Adjective meaning out of the ordinary (che straordinario odore).
Used as a masculine plural noun in the workplace for overtime.
Fourth month of the year; lowercase in Italian.
Coordinating conjunction introducing contrast or surprise (ma guarda!, ma come?).

examples.trans: I wanted to come, but I am working.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner/pronoun; before masculine nouns adapts like lo/il: quel, quell', quello, quei, quegli.

examples.trans: Do you see those light stands?

meanings.note: Both a narrative and an old dispute or affair.
Unit of calendar time; used with avere to state someone's age.
Links words or clauses; distinct from accented è, meaning is.
Agrees in sette e mezza (sc. mezza ora, 'half an hour' -> 7:30); masculine in un anno e mezzo.

examples.text: Ci vediamo alle sette e mezza.

examples.trans: I have been waiting half an hour.

meanings.note: Placed after a time span (un anno fa, 'a year ago'); historically from fare.

examples.trans: A year and a half ago.

meanings.note: Confirms and sharpens what the previous speaker just said.
Normally takes a direct object, without the English preposition for.
Anticipate something happening.

examples.trans: I am waiting for a friend.

meanings.note: Everyday Italian treats 'money' as masculine plural: quei soldi.

examples.trans: I have no money on me.

meanings.note: Third-person masculine plural direct object pronoun before the verb.
Irregular future vedrete ('you all will see') and past participle visto ('seen / watched').

examples.trans: Do you see those light stands?

meanings.note: Follows a verb negated by non (non parli mai, 'you never speak').
Builds general statements (non si fuma, i copioni si cambiano).
Third-person reflexive pronoun (si chiama, si è svegliata, non si preoccupi).
Core verb used in many idioms: non fa niente, fare schifo, farsi la doccia, fare il bravo.
Points to the manner in which something is done.

examples.trans: One does not behave like that.

meanings.note: Marks constant repetition or habit.
È sempre uguale shrugs that nothing ever changes.
Emphasises the whole course or experience of a day, as in Buona giornata!

examples.trans: It has been a long day.
